title: Quickstart 'Slate' assets for rollouts: pinning, canary, A/B, and fallback visuals
creator: Maya Patel
description: Design a compact quickstart 'Slate' — a set of polished, copy-ready UX assets and annotated screenshots that introduce Rollouts and Version Pinning in the console. The slate targets new engineers and product folks doing first-time setup: a single-page visual walkthrough plus a set of modular screenshot assets for docs, in-product help, and the onboarding email template. Assets cover: the pin modal, canary creation wizard, A/B split editor, fallback policy editor, simulation overlay (traffic simulator), and the success/failure states for pin and rollout changes.
goals: Create a minimal, scannable quickstart visual (single-pane) that users can read in under 90 seconds
Provide modular screenshot assets for docs and marketing (desktop 1440x900 and tablet 1024x768 variants)
Standardize copy and microcopy for pinning, canary, A/B splits, and fallback policy language
Deliver annotated Figma pages and export-ready PNG/SVG assets for engineering docs and the in-app help widget
deliverables: Single-page Quickstart PDF (1-2 pages) with progressive disclosure flows
Figma file: Rollouts Quickstart Slate (frames: Landing, Pin modal, Canary wizard, A/B editor, Fallback editor, Simulator overlay)
Set of exported screenshots (desktop/tablet) + alt text and captions
Motion spec for subtle transitions in the canary slider and A/B split editor
Copy doc with microcopy options (short, friendly, and technical tone variants)
screenshots_needed: Quickstart landing panel with 3-step checklist and CTA
Pin override modal (with version dropdown and pin scope selector)
Canary creation wizard: traffic slider + preview sample responses panel
A/B split editor: branch naming, weight inputs, explanation tooltip
Fallback policy editor: prioritized fallbacks list and automatic fallback toggle
Traffic simulator overlay: run simulation button, results summary, latency/cost estimates
Toast success and rollback confirmation modal
Error states: failed rollout due to capacity, invalid model version, permission denied
acceptance_criteria: All frames exported in desktop/tablet sizes and validated against copy doc
Microcopy reviewed and approved by PM (Lucas Chen) and Eng reviewer (Priya Nair)
Figma file includes annotations for QA and screenshot crop guides
Assets delivered to docs drive and linked from the PRD before merge
Accessibility: alt text provided for every screenshot, color contrast meets AA
updates: 2025-02-10: Ticket created by Maya — scoped slate to accelerate new-user rollouts onboarding.

2025-02-12: Initial whiteboard concept reviewed with PM Lucas Chen — decided to prefer a single-pane quickstart with optional deep links to each flow rather than separate multi-step wizards (trade-off: fewer screenshots, clearer onboarding).
2025-02-13: Figma roughs uploaded (link in mockups). Requested: add sample response panel in canary wizard to show observable quality differences between model variants.
2025-02-14: Engineering review (Priya Nair) — noted runtime metrics for traffic simulator should show both latency and estimated cost; asked for a disabled state when no capacity is available.

2025-02-16: Design review with Zoe Martinez — approved visual language; asked to tighten microcopy around 'pin scope' to avoid implying permanent changes. Action: provide two microcopy options (friendly + technical).
2025-02-17: Figma final frames exported to Drive; motion spec drafted for canary slider. Uploaded PNGs for docs placeholder: https://drive.google.com/rollouts/quickstart/exports
2025-02-18: PRD link and screenshots attached to this ticket. Ready for PM sign-off and engineering QA for final alt text and crop validation.
feedback: Lucas Chen (PM): 'Love single-pane approach — reduces cognitive load for first-time users. Ensure we call out safety guardrails for canaries.'
Priya Nair (Eng): 'Simulator needs to show estimated GPU cost per 1M tokens and average p95 latency. Provide a collapsed metrics row for compact view.'
Zoe Martinez (Design Lead): 'Motion should be subtle; avoid adding new UI affordances. Keep CTA hierarchy consistent with other console quickstarts.'
risks_and_tradeoffs: Single-pane quickstart reduces hand-holding depth; complex cases will still need deeper docs — we will include 'advanced' deep-link anchors in the PDF and help panel.
Simulator estimated costs are heuristics; must include clear disclaimer and link to cost explainer in docs.
Providing multiple microcopy tones increases review overhead but improves downstream reuse in marketing and docs.
next_steps: Request PM sign-off on final microcopy (assigned to Lucas Chen).
Create a small engineering PR to add screenshot crop endpoints and alt text hooks (owner: frontend infra).
Finalize motion spec and hand off to frontend with token-level animation timing values.
Upload final exports to docs drive and add links to the PRD before the release branch cut.
